name: An
notes: Oan, daughter of Yamada Kyoreki (retainer of Ishida Mitsunari), lived through the 1600 siege of Ogaki and dictated the Oan monogatari; kotobank: 江戸時代前期の女性; o- prefix stripped

name: Riku
notes: Oishi Riku (1669-1736), wife of Oishi Yoshio of Ako; kotobank: 寛文9年生まれ

name: Etsu
notes: Endo Etsu (1814-1862), wife of a village headman heir in Nagabe village, Katori, Shimosa; kotobank: 文化11年生まれ, 江戸時代後期の女性 - a dated commoner bearer for a form previously held only from register lists

name: Ate
notes: Keikoin (1666-1683), wife of Asano Tsunanaga of Hiroshima, third daughter of Tokugawa Mitsutomo of Owari; article: 実名は貴姫（あてひめ）- hime honorific stripped

name: Atsuko
notes: Takatsukasa Atsuko (1823-1848), first wife of the future shogun Tokugawa Iesada; also Saisho Atsuko (1825-1900), poet and court lady, and Matsumuro Atsuko (d. 1746), consort of Emperor Reigen - three bearers, all born before 1868

name: Itsuki
notes: Honkoin (d. 1710), concubine of shogun Tokugawa Ienobu; article: 俗名は斎宮（いつきのみや）。名はいつき、または園

name: Inui
notes: Ganshoin (d. 1527), wife of Oda Nobusada and grandmother of Oda Nobunaga; article: 名はいぬゐ (historical kana wi)

name: Ioko
notes: Okumura Ioko (1845-1907), social activist, founder of the Aikoku Fujinkai; born Koka 2 in Karatsu

name: Iwashiro
notes: Oe Iwashiro (1744-1813), lady of Prince Kan-in Sukehito and mother of Emperor Kokaku; commoner-born (Kurayoshi, Hoki)

name: Ikuko
notes: Ichijo Ikuko (1729-1808), wife of Tokugawa Munemoto of Mito; also Noma Ikuko (1849-1946), concubine of Kujo Michitaka and grandmother of Emperor Showa

name: Izumi
notes: Okun (1715-1780), concubine of Tokugawa Muneharu of Owari; article gives 別名に和泉（いづみ）- an alternate personal name, not a court office here

name: Ryoko
notes: Mutsu Ryoko (1856-1900), wife of Mutsu Munemitsu; also Yoshimasu Ryoko (1857-1886), one of the first Japanese women students abroad

name: Reiko
notes: Hashimoto Reiko, daughter of Hashimoto Saneakira, court lady (Dainagon no suke) in Kazunomiya's retinue, Wikidata birth 1835; the same kanji is read reishi for Onmeimon-in (1185-1243) in kotobank

name: Aguri
notes: Oto Aguri (b. 1648), wife of Makino Narisada of Sekiyado; firmer attestation for a form previously held only from the low-confidence note.com Sengoku dictionary

name: Aku
notes: Shoan Kenkyu-ni (1538-1585), Azai clan woman; article: 名は阿久（あく）- firmer attestation for a form already in raw

name: Ejima
notes: Ejima (1681-1741), otoshiyori of the Ooku under Gekkoin, central figure of the 1714 Ejima-Ikushima affair; SERVICE NAME (女中名) - her birth name is not recorded; also borne by a later attendant listed on 和宮付き大奥女中

name: Ikushima
notes: Ikushima (1808-1870), otoshiyori who accompanied Tenshoin (Atsuhime) into the Ooku; SERVICE NAME (女中名), birth name not given

name: Utahashi
url: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/徳川家定付き大奥女中
notes: Utahashi, joro-otoshiyori and wet-nurse of shogun Tokugawa Iesada (active 1850s, so born well before 1868); SERVICE NAME (女中名)

name: Iwao
notes: Iwao, chief otoshiyori attending Honjuin (mother of Iesada), active 1850s-60s; SERVICE NAME (女中名), dates unknown

name: Rai
notes: Okuda (Oshima) Raikin, Kyoto townswoman painter and seal-carver, dates unknown but exhibited among late-Edo women painters; leaflet: 名を蘿井といい - READING INFERRED (on-yomi rai), the leaflet gives no furigana; verify before promoting
